climate.overview_html: COP31 opens in Antalya in five days. The Pacific Pre-COP in Fiji and Tuvalu concluded with the Taku Pakasoa Declaration, backing faster emissions cuts, accessible climate finance and strengthened ocean protection. The African Group has formally pushed for a dedicated agenda item on adaptation finance, raising the risk of a procedural fight on the summit’s opening day. WMO’s latest ocean update projects the 2026 El Niño Niño 3.4 anomaly peaking near +3.7°C in December—the strongest El Niño on record by this metric, surpassing the previous +2.6°C record set in November 2015–January 2016. The official Copernicus C3S October 2026 monthly bulletin—expected to confirm October as the warmest on record at ~1.76°C above preindustrial—remained unpublished as of November 4.

items.headline: Pacific Pre-COP Concludes with Taku Pakasoa Declaration: Faster Emissions Cuts, Accessible Climate Finance, Ocean Protection
items.summary: The Pacific Pre-COP, with government meetings in Fiji and a leaders' retreat in Tuvalu, concluded with the Taku Pakasoa Declaration. Pacific leaders — among the most climate-vulnerable nations — called for accelerated emissions reductions consistent with 1.5°C, more accessible and direct climate finance for small island developing states, and strengthened protection of oceans as a global climate regulator. The declaration aligned with the COP31 Presidency's agenda of launching electrification pledges and adding ocean protection to the summit programme on Energy Day, November 10.

items.headline: African Group Pushes for Dedicated COP31 Agenda Item on Adaptation Finance, Raising Risk of Opening-Day Procedural Fight
items.summary: The African Group of Negotiators has formally requested a standalone agenda item on adaptation finance at COP31, alongside progress items on the Green Climate Fund and trade. Developed countries, particularly the EU, have resisted a formal agenda item, preferring adaptation to be addressed within the broader New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG) framework. If parties cannot agree on the agenda at the summit's opening plenary, it could trigger procedural fights that have derailed COP sessions in the past. Africa's demand reflects frustration that only about 20% of climate finance flows to adaptation globally.

items.headline: WMO: 2026 El Niño Niño 3.4 Projected to Peak Near +3.7°C in December—Strongest Ever Recorded; Previous Record +2.6°C (2015–16)
items.summary: WMO's October ocean temperature update confirms the 2026 El Niño is the strongest on record by several metrics. The Niño 3.4 index anomaly is projected to peak near +3.7°C in October–December 2026, surpassing the previous record of +2.6°C set in November 2015–January 2016 by over 1°C. The event is driving record global surface temperatures, the exceptional 2026 Atlantic and Pacific tropical cyclone seasons, the Bay of Bengal back-to-back cyclone sequence, the prolonged Southeast Asian peatland fire crisis, and the 13 consecutive months above 1.5°C. WMO warns that peak impacts on regional precipitation patterns may not arrive until 2027 during the La Niña transition.

items.headline: Canada Positions Itself as COP31 Climate Leader Despite Policy Rollbacks; PM Carney Skips Leaders Segment; Methane Mitigation Focus
items.summary: Canada's delegation at COP31 is promoting the country as a climate leader even as PM Mark Carney skips the November 11–12 world leaders segment; Environment Minister Julie Dabrusin will attend the first week in his place. Canada plans to highlight methane mitigation as its flagship contribution, while domestic critics point to rollbacks on clean fuel regulations and carbon pricing.

items.headline: EU Climate Chief Hoekstra: COP31 Finance Talks ‘Dead in the Water’; Mobilised Climate Finance at $136.7 Billion vs. $300 Billion Goal
items.summary: EU Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra told Bloomberg that talks on new climate finance commitments at COP31 are 'dead in the water,' arguing major new pledges must come from outside the EU. Developed-country mobilised climate finance reached $136.7 billion in 2025 against a $300 billion-per-year 2035 goal. The Pilot Resilience Fund — meant to raise $500 million by COP31 — has secured only $180 million in pledges.

items.headline: NDC Synthesis Report: Full Implementation of All Current NDCs Still Leads to 2.3–2.5°C Warming by 2100—~1°C Above the Paris Limit
items.summary: A Böll Foundation analysis of the UNFCCC NDC Synthesis Report finds that even full implementation of every NDC submitted ahead of COP31 would still result in 2.3–2.5°C above preindustrial levels by 2100 — roughly 1°C above the Paris 1.5°C limit. The analysis stresses that the absence of credible climate finance commitments directly undermines developing countries' ability to submit more ambitious NDCs.

items.headline: October 2026 Projected Warmest October on Record at ~1.76°C Above Preindustrial; 13th Consecutive Month Above 1.5°C; Official C3S Bulletin Pending
items.summary: October 2026 closed as the projected warmest October in the ERA5 instrumental record at approximately 1.76°C above preindustrial averages, driven by the record 2026 El Niño. The result marks the 13th consecutive month with global temperatures above the 1.5°C Paris threshold. The official Copernicus C3S monthly climate bulletin for October had not been published as of November 4.

items.headline: UN Deputy Secretary-General: ‘Overshoot Is Not a Reason to Surrender’ Climate Ambition; Loss and Damage Fund Operationalisation Urged Ahead of COP31
items.summary: UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed called on governments not to use potential 1.5°C overshoot as a rationale for withdrawing climate commitments, stressing that the window to limit catastrophic warming remains open. She called for accelerated emissions cuts, increased adaptation investment, and full operationalisation of the Loss and Damage Fund ahead of COP31.

items.headline: Nepal and Bhutan Propose Dedicated COP31 Agenda Item on 1.5°C Warming in Mountain Regions; Nepal Pushes ‘Sagarmatha to Sea’ Alliance
items.summary: Nepal's Agriculture, Forests and Environment Minister Geeta Chaudhary presented a joint Nepal–Bhutan proposal for a dedicated COP31 agenda item on '1.5°C Warming in Mountains,' citing ICIMOD research showing mountain elevations experience warming rates up to 2.2°C for every 1.5°C of global mean warming. Nepal also proposed the 'Sagarmatha to Sea' partnership linking Himalayan and Pacific island states on shared risks from glacial melt and sea-level rise.

major_events.name: Cyclone Murasu — Dissipating Inland Over Andhra Pradesh / Telangana; Residual Flooding Easing
major_events.status: Post-landfall dissipation — system crossed Andhra Pradesh coast early November 3 and is now weakening rapidly inland; tens of thousands remain displaced with infrastructure damage assessment ongoing; residual heavy rains expected to ease through November 5
major_events.impact: Murasu is the second Bay of Bengal named cyclone to make landfall on the Andhra Pradesh coastline in under six days, following Cyclone Arnab on October 28 — an unprecedented back-to-back sequence driven by anomalously warm Bay of Bengal SSTs linked to the record-intensity 2026 El Niño. Combined damage from both storms has compounded stress on coastal infrastructure, agricultural zones, and inland river systems.

major_events.name: Florida Extreme Flooding — Rivers in Flood Stage Through Weekend; NWS Active Warnings Brevard, Volusia, West-Central Counties
major_events.status: Active river flooding — NWS Melbourne issued Flood Warning for St. Johns River near Astor in moderate flood stage through the weekend; NWS Tampa Bay warns Peace, Alafia and Manatee rivers remain in flood stage following 5–10 inches of rain across west-central Florida; acute flash flood emergency phase has ended, transitioning to slow-drain river flood pattern
major_events.impact: Following the November 2 extreme rainfall event (up to 15 inches in Brevard County, 6–12 inches Treasure Coast), rivers across east and west-central Florida remain elevated. The simultaneous November 2 king-tide surge along South Florida's coastline has receded, though some seawalls and low-lying roads remain compromised. Governor's state of emergency remains in effect.

major_events.name: Southwest US Flooding Aftermath — Active Cleanup in Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico; More Than 10 All-Time Flood Records Broken
major_events.status: Recovery — extreme atmospheric river event from November 1–2 has ended; active cleanup and damage assessment underway across Flagstaff, Sedona, Tucson, Durango and Pagosa Springs; more than 10 all-time flood gauge records broken across three states; smaller stream flooding continues in some areas
major_events.impact: The Four Corners atmospheric river produced historic flooding across Arizona, Nevada and the Southwest. Separately, 19 inches fell in six hours near the Louisiana border in southwest Mississippi — a simultaneous extreme event pointing to an exceptional large-scale moisture pattern. Attribution research is expected to examine the role of the record 2026 El Niño-elevated SSTs in amplifying atmospheric moisture flux.

major_events.name: Southeast Asian Peatland Haze (Indonesia / Borneo / Sumatra) — Ongoing; ~40 Million Exposed; Wet Season Transition Underway
major_events.status: Ongoing, slow easing — wet season onset beginning in some areas of Sumatra and Kalimantan is reducing surface fire intensity, but underground peat fires at depths up to 8 m continue and are extremely difficult to extinguish; bilateral Indonesia–Singapore task force remains operational; more than 333,470 acute respiratory cases across seven Indonesian provinces recorded
major_events.impact: ~40 million people region-wide continue to experience elevated PM2.5. The El Niño peak in December threatens to further delay the wet-season transition in the most fire-prone peatland areas, potentially extending the haze crisis into late November. The fires have produced an estimated CO₂ release that will register as a measurable atmospheric spike in November–December ERA5 data.

weather.overview_html: Cyclone Murasu is now dissipating inland after its November 3 landfall on the Andhra Pradesh coast, with damage assessment and displaced-population recovery ongoing. In the US, the acute Florida flooding emergency has transitioned to a slow-drain river flood pattern with NWS active warnings for the St. Johns, Peace, Alafia and Manatee rivers through at least November 4–7. The Southwest atmospheric river has ended and cleanup is underway across Arizona, Colorado and New Mexico. In the western Pacific, Typhoon In-fa has weakened to 75 kt and is tracking northwestward away from the Philippines, with no PAR entry expected.

items.headline: NWS Active Flood Warnings: St. Johns River Near Astor in Moderate Flood Stage Through Weekend; Peace, Alafia and Manatee Rivers Remain Elevated in West-Central Florida
items.summary: NWS Melbourne (FL) issued a Flood Warning for the St. Johns River near Astor in Volusia and Lake counties, with the river in moderate flood stage and canals overflowing into yards; heavy upstream rainfall will maintain river levels through the weekend. NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin separately warned that the Peace, Alafia and Manatee rivers in west-central Florida remain in flood stage following 5–10 inches of regional rainfall, with stages expected to remain elevated over several days. The acute flash flood emergency phase for Brevard County has ended, transitioning to a slower-moving river flood pattern.

items.headline: Cyclone Murasu Makes Landfall on Andhra Pradesh Coast Early November 3; Tens of Thousands Displaced; Extensive Damage; System Weakening Inland
items.summary: Cyclone Murasu crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur as a severe cyclonic storm with maximum sustained winds of 100–110 km/h (gusts to 120 km/h) early on November 3, causing extensive damage and displacing tens of thousands. As of November 4 the system is dissipating inland. Murasu is the second Bay of Bengal named cyclone to hit the same general coastline in under six days following Cyclone Arnab's October 28 landfall.

items.source: Fox Weather / Yale Climate Connections / NWS
items.headline: 1,000-Year Flooding Hits Brevard County Florida; Governor Declares Emergency; NWS Flash Flood Emergency for West Melbourne and Palm Bay; Historic King Tides in South Florida
items.summary: NWS offices in Melbourne and Miami issued flash flood emergencies for multiple Florida counties on November 2 following extreme rainfall: up to 15 inches in Brevard County, 6–12 inches along the Treasure Coast. Florida's governor declared a state of emergency citing a 1,000-year flood event for parts of Brevard County. Historic king tides overwhelmed South Florida seawalls and flooded major roads and bridges. No tropical system was active near Florida.

items.headline: Simultaneous 1,000-Year Flooding in Southwest US and Southwest Mississippi; 10+ All-Time Flood Gauge Records Broken; 19 Inches in Six Hours Near Louisiana Border
items.summary: The same November 2 extreme atmospheric moisture event produced record flooding across Arizona, Nevada and the Four Corners region, breaking all-time records at more than 10 flood gauges in three states. A separate event in southwest Mississippi produced 19 inches of rainfall in six hours, also described as a 1,000-year occurrence. Cleanup and damage assessment are underway; attribution research expected to examine the role of El Niño-elevated SSTs.

items.headline: Typhoon In-fa Weakens to 75 kt, Tracking Away from Philippines; PAR Entry Risk Remains Low
items.summary: Typhoon In-fa has weakened to approximately 75 kt (down from 155 km/h on November 1), moving northwestward and now located well east-northeast of the Philippines and tracking away from the region into higher-latitude, cooler waters. PAGASA maintains a low probability of PAR entry. The storm is expected to continue weakening.

items.headline: Southeast Asian Peatland Haze: Indonesia–Singapore Task Force Active; ~40 Million Exposed; Underground Peat Fires at 8 m Depth Continuing Even as Wet Season Begins
items.summary: The 2026 Southeast Asian peatland haze crisis continues. Underground peat fires at depths up to 8 metres resist wet-season rain onset across Sumatra and Kalimantan. ~40 million people exposed to elevated PM2.5 across Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore. 333,470+ acute respiratory cases across seven Indonesian provinces. The Indonesia–Singapore bilateral task force remains operational. The El Niño peak in December threatens to extend the crisis into late November.

items.headline: Cyclone Arnab Aftermath: Landfall Oct 28 Near Yanam, Andhra Pradesh; 3+ Deaths; Strongest Post-Monsoon Bay of Bengal Cyclone Since 2014
items.summary: Cyclone Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast near Yanam during October 28 as a 'very severe cyclonic storm' with maximum sustained winds of 125–135 km/h and gusts to 150 km/h — the first named cyclone of the 2026 North Indian Ocean season and the strongest post-monsoon Bay of Bengal storm since 2014. At least three deaths and approximately 180,000 evacuations were reported. The rapid follow-on cyclogenesis of Murasu within six days reflects record-warm Bay SSTs of the 2026 El Niño season.

renewables.overview_html: BW Energy Storage Systems acquired two 100 MW/400 MWh BESS projects in France from Recurrent Energy (Canadian Solar), marking BW ESS’s entry into its seventh global market. In Australia, Squadron Energy received state planning approval for its 420 MW Moreton Hill wind farm in Victoria. India’s NHPC and Essar Renewables announced a $475 million hybrid solar, wind and BESS partnership in Andhra Pradesh. At the ongoing Bharat Renewable Energy Summit 2026, officials confirmed India’s non-fossil electricity capacity has surpassed 310 GW, meeting its Paris target five years early.

items.headline: BW ESS Acquires Two 100 MW/400 MWh BESS Projects in France from Recurrent Energy (Canadian Solar); Enters Seventh Global Market
items.summary: BW Energy Storage Systems completed the acquisition of two standalone BESS projects in France from Recurrent Energy (a Canadian Solar subsidiary): 100 MW/400 MWh at Baixas (Eastern Pyrenees) and 100 MW/400 MWh at Coquainvilliers (Calvados), combined 200 MW/800 MWh. The deal marks BW ESS's entry into France, its seventh market globally (alongside the UK, Italy, Germany, Spain, Australia and the US). BW ESS's CEO described the acquisition as complementing France's nuclear-based generation with large-scale rapid-response battery flexibility.

items.headline: Squadron Energy Receives State Planning Approval for 420 MW Moreton Hill Wind Farm in Victoria, Australia; Up to 62 Turbines
items.summary: Squadron Energy, one of Australia's largest renewable energy developers, received state planning approval for its 420 MW Moreton Hill wind farm in Victoria, which will incorporate up to 62 wind turbines. The approval is a key development milestone for the project, contributing to Australia's target of 82% renewable electricity by 2030.

items.headline: NHPC and Essar Renewables to Partner on $475 Million Hybrid Renewable Energy Project in Andhra Pradesh; Solar, Wind and Battery Storage
items.summary: India's National Hydroelectric Power Corporation (NHPC) and Essar Renewables announced a partnership to develop a $475 million hybrid renewable energy project in Andhra Pradesh, integrating solar PV, wind and battery energy storage systems to supply renewable power. The deal builds on existing collaboration between the two companies in state-awarded RE tenders and aligns with Andhra Pradesh's aggressive renewable energy expansion targets.

items.headline: PM Modi Opens Bharat Renewable Energy Summit 2026: India Crosses 310 GW Non-Fossil Capacity, Meets Paris Target 5 Years Early; 500 GW Additional by 2030
items.summary: PM Modi inaugurated the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit 2026 (November 2–5, New Delhi), announcing India has surpassed 310 GW of non-fossil power capacity (>50% of total installed power), meeting its Paris Agreement climate commitment five years ahead of schedule. Solar capacity grew from 2.8 GW to 171 GW; wind from 21 GW to 60 GW. Modi set an additional 500 GW non-fossil capacity target by 2030–2031.

items.headline: Solar Sector Corporate Funding Up 45% Year-on-Year Through Three Quarters of 2026; 88 M&A Transactions in 9M 2026 vs. 76 in 9M 2025
items.summary: Solar sector corporate funding rose 45% year-on-year through the first three quarters of 2026, per PV Magazine analysis. The sector recorded 88 M&A transactions in 9M 2026, up from 76 in 9M 2025. Notable deals included Inox Solar Americas' $750 million purchase of Boviet Solar and Drax's $737 million acquisition of Bluefield Solar Income Fund. Growth reflects sustained data-centre and industrial load demand for clean energy capacity.

items.headline: US Interior Dept Seeks Court Reconsideration of Permits for Four Major Offshore Wind Projects Including 704 MW Revolution Wind and 1.7 GW Maryland Offshore Wind
items.summary: The US Interior and Justice Departments have sought court reconsideration of construction and operations plan approvals for at least four East Coast offshore wind projects: the 704 MW Revolution Wind (partly operational), the 1.7 GW Maryland Offshore Wind project, Atlantic Shores (NJ) and New England Wind (MA). ~300 wind and solar projects also await Department of Defense review.

items.headline: India’s SECI Launches Largest-Yet 4 GW/16 GWh Standalone Battery Storage Tender for Rajasthan and Gujarat; Bid Deadline November 24
items.summary: India's Solar Energy Corporation (SECI) invited bids for 4,000 MW/16,000 MWh of standalone BESS — 2,500 MW/10,000 MWh in Rajasthan and 1,500 MW/6,000 MWh in Gujarat — its largest standalone BESS tender to date. Bid deadline: November 24. Directly supports India's 27,000 MW BESS capacity target by FY2030.

items.headline: Equinor Delays 810 MW Empire Wind First Power to H1 2027 Due to US Shipbuilding Constraints; Total Capex Unchanged
items.summary: Equinor's 810 MW Empire Wind project off New York — approximately 80% complete — will not deliver first power until H1 2027, delayed from a 2026 target, due to US domestic shipbuilding requirements for installation support vessels. Total capex is unchanged; $3 billion+ project financing package is in place.

items.headline: South Korea Launches Second 2026 Offshore Wind Tender: ~2.2 GW Fixed-Price Contracts; 10-Year Annual Auction Roadmap Through 2035 Published
items.summary: South Korea's Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment launched competitive bidding for approximately 2.2 GW of offshore wind fixed-price contracts, the country's second auction of 2026. The H1 2026 round was oversubscribed at more than 2:1. The government published its Offshore Wind Mid-to-Long-Term Bidding Roadmap, targeting a minimum of 4 GW in annual auctions through 2035.

items.headline: UK Grants Development Consent for 800 MW Great North Road Solar Farm in Nottinghamshire—One of UK’s Largest-Ever Solar Project Approvals
items.summary: The UK government granted a Development Consent Order for the 800 MW Great North Road Solar Farm in Nottinghamshire (developer: Elements Green), approved as a Nationally Significant Infrastructure Project covering approximately 1,765 hectares near Newark.

items.headline: First Solar Q3 2026: Cuts Full-Year Guidance, Launches $500 M Share Buyback; Record Adjusted EBITDA Margins Despite 23% Revenue Decline
items.summary: First Solar reported Q3 2026 net sales of $1.23 billion (down 23% year-on-year), net income of $571 million, and record adjusted EBITDA of $744 million (up 11%). Board authorised a $500 million share buyback. Full-year guidance lowered; contracted backlog stands at 44 GW ($13.5 billion). Stock has fallen 45% from its June 2026 high.

science.overview_html: WMO’s latest ocean update projects the 2026 El Niño Niño 3.4 anomaly peaking near +3.7°C in December—the strongest El Niño ever recorded by this metric and over 1°C above the previous 2015–16 record. A new arXiv preprint benchmarks GenCast, FourCastNet 3 and FGN against IFS-ENS for tropical cyclone probabilistic forecasting, with AI models outperforming on track but showing uneven intensity skill. ECMWF’s AIFS-COMPO remains the standout operational milestone of the week. In climate physics, a GRL study confirms accelerating Arctic warming is weakening the boreal carbon sink, while HRRRCast and FitzRoy continue to represent the leading edge of regional ML forecasting preprints from the past seven days.

items.headline: WMO: 2026 El Niño Niño 3.4 Projected to Peak Near +3.7°C in December—Strongest Ever Recorded; Previous Record +2.6°C (2015–16)
items.summary: WMO's October ocean temperature update confirms the 2026 El Niño is the strongest on record by several metrics. The Niño 3.4 index anomaly is projected to peak near +3.7°C in October–December 2026, surpassing the previous record of +2.6°C set in November 2015–January 2016 by over 1°C. The event is driving record global surface temperatures, the exceptional 2026 cyclone seasons in multiple basins, and the prolonged Southeast Asian peatland fire crisis. WMO warns that peak impacts on regional precipitation patterns may not arrive until 2027 during the La Niña transition.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.22077 — Can AI Forecast the Extremes? Benchmarking GenCast, FourCastNet 3 and FGN Against IFS-ENS for Tropical Cyclone Probabilistic Forecasting
items.summary: A preprint benchmarks three probabilistic AI weather models — GenCast, FourCastNet 3 and FGN — against ECMWF's IFS-ENS on tropical cyclone forecasting for 2025. AI models outperform IFS-ENS on track (location) scores, with FGN winning probabilistic location skill for 90% of storms evaluated. Intensity prediction remains an open challenge for all AI models. The study directly addresses whether AI weather models are ready for operational use in high-stakes extreme-event scenarios — a critical adoption hurdle given the record 2026 cyclone season.

items.headline: ECMWF Introduces AIFS-COMPO: AI System Extends Neural Weather Forecasting to Aerosols and Reactive Gases; 10-Day Global Air Quality Forecasts in 50 Seconds per GPU
items.meta: Alexe et al. (ECMWF) · arXiv:2604.03300 · Experimental operational deployment October 2026
items.summary: ECMWF's experimental AIFS-COMPO system jointly predicts meteorological variables and atmospheric composition — aerosols (AOD, PM2.5) and reactive gases (ozone, NO2). It produces 3-hourly, 10-day global forecasts in 50 seconds on a single GPU, vs. ~1,000 seconds on 8,000 CPUs for operational IFS-COMPO. AIFS-COMPO achieves lower errors than IFS-COMPO for 5-day AOD and PM2.5 forecasts. Remains experimental — not replacing operational CAMS.

items.headline: GRL: Accelerating Arctic Warming Now Inhibiting Net Land Carbon Uptake in Northern High Latitudes—Boreal Carbon Sink Weakening Signal
items.meta: Madani et al. · Geophysical Research Letters doi:10.1029/2026GL122135
items.summary: A GRL study finds that progressive warming is inhibiting net land carbon uptake in northern high latitudes, with moisture deficits, heightened soil respiration, and permafrost carbon release outpacing vegetation productivity gains. The findings signal measurable weakening of the Arctic and boreal carbon sink — a major carbon feedback — reinforcing the need to represent permafrost carbon processes in IPCC-class Earth system models and AI climate emulators targeting decadal projections.

items.headline: GRL: ‘Permafrost Detachment Slides’—Climate-Driven Bottom-Up Failure Mode—Expected to Become More Frequent; 150+ Documented in Mackenzie Valley
items.summary: A GRL study identifies 'permafrost detachment slides' as a distinct bottom-up failure mechanism: slides fail from the base upward due to decades of ~0.3°C/decade permafrost warming combined with historic wildfire disturbance. The Mackenzie Valley alone has more than 150 such slides. Events of this type will become more frequent with continued warming, with implications for Arctic communities and infrastructure.

items.headline: China CMA Deploys Two Operational AI Weather Systems: Typhoon Cloud-Pattern Recognition and 4-Hour Severe Convective Prediction Using Fengyun Satellite Data
items.summary: China's Meteorological Administration unveiled two new operational AI weather systems: a typhoon cloud-pattern recognition model interpreting storm structure from Fengyun satellite imagery in real time, and a model predicting severe convective weather up to four hours in advance. Both are deployed operationally within the CMA's national forecast suite.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.40641 — Agentic AI Framework Connects Extreme-Weather Probabilistic Forecasts to Agricultural and Adaptation Impact Estimates End-to-End
items.summary: An agentic AI framework couples a weather-event detection module with an agricultural impact model, enabling automated end-to-end assessment from probabilistic forecast output to expected crop, livestock or infrastructure effects in near-real-time — addressing the critical gap between high-impact weather warnings and sector-specific impact projections.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.38775 — FitzRoy: Reinforcement-Guided Diffusion Model Jointly Optimises Forecast Skill and Physical Realism for Continental US Precipitation
items.summary: FitzRoy applies reinforcement-guided diffusion to precipitation forecasting over the continental US, jointly optimising predictive skill and physical realism via a reinforcement learning reward signal. Standard diffusion-based weather models trade off sharp but physically implausible fields against smooth oversmoothed outputs; FitzRoy's RL guidance drives the diffusion process toward physically consistent outputs while retaining skill. Evaluated against MRMS radar observations and standard probabilistic metrics.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.36186 — HRRRCast: First Data-Driven Regional Weather Model to Match NOAA’s Operational HRRR on Extreme Events in Near-Real-Time
items.summary: HRRRCast is the first data-driven regional weather model demonstrated to match the skill of NOAA's operational HRRR on extreme weather events while running in near-real-time. Validated against severe convective outbreaks and extreme precipitation episodes; describes an operational deployment pathway for hybrid HRRR/HRRRCast products.

items.headline: Google DeepMind AI Model Beat Physics-Based Forecasts on Hurricane Isaias Track—Correctly Forecast Florida Panhandle Landfall Where Physics Models Said Louisiana; Intensity Gap Persists
items.summary: Google DeepMind's AI weather model outperformed traditional physics-based models on the track forecast for Hurricane Isaias (Category 2, Florida Panhandle landfall), correctly indicating the Florida Panhandle while physics-based models pointed to Louisiana. ECMWF's AIFS showed the second-strongest track performance in the 2026 Atlantic season. AI trailed the NHC's blended consensus on intensity — a persistent gap. Interpretability concerns remain.

items.title: BW ESS Acquires 200 MW/800 MWh French Battery Storage Portfolio from Recurrent Energy (Canadian Solar)—Enters Seventh Global Market
items.body_html: BW Energy Storage Systems acquired two ready-to-build standalone BESS projects in France from Canadian Solar’s subsidiary Recurrent Energy, comprising a 100 MW/400 MWh project at Baixas (Eastern Pyrénées) and a second 100 MW/400 MWh project at Coquainvilliers (Calvados). The deal marks BW ESS’s entry into France, its seventh market globally, adding to existing positions in the UK, Italy, Germany, Spain, Australia and the US. BW ESS’s CEO described the projects as complementing France’s predominantly nuclear grid with large-scale rapid-response battery flexibility.

items.title: CESC/Purvah Green Extends ReNew 1.4 GWp Acquisition Deadline to November 21—~$510 M Deal Still Pending
items.body_html: India’s CESC Limited and its renewable arm Purvah Green Power have amended the share purchase agreement for their ~1.4 GWp ReNew Solar Power acquisition, extending the closing deadline 21 days to November 21, 2026. The deal covers six SPVs holding approximately 1.4 GWp of contracted operating solar capacity at an enterprise value of ~₹4,859 crore (~US$510 million), with more than 90% contracted with SECI.

items.title: Vaisala Completes Acquisition of AI Weather Company Atmo, Inc.—USD 70 M Fixed + Up to USD 60 M Earn-Out; Deepens AI Forecasting Strategy
items.body_html: Finnish measurement technology leader Vaisala completed the acquisition of AI weather forecasting company Atmo, Inc. on October 29, four months after announcing the deal. The fixed purchase price was USD 70 million, with a contingent earn-out of up to USD 60 million tied to 2026–2028 performance targets. The deal “supports Vaisala’s strategic priority to grow its services and software revenue” alongside its traditional hardware and sensor businesses.

items.title: Boralex Acquires UK Onshore Wind Developer Wind2—~350 MW Advanced Pipeline in Scotland, England and Wales; Lifts UK Portfolio to ~2 GW
items.body_html: Canadian renewable producer Boralex completed the acquisition of UK onshore wind developer Wind2 on October 29, adding approximately 350 MW of advanced-stage projects across Scotland, England and Wales and lifting its total UK development pipeline to approximately 2 GW alongside 73 MW under construction. Boralex was taken private by La Caisse de dépôt et placement du Québec in August 2026.

items.title: Equitix Completes £155 M Beatrice Offshore Wind Stake Purchase from TRIG—Now 35% Owner of 588 MW Scottish Project; TRIG Fully Exits
items.body_html: Equitix completed the purchase of TRIG’s 17.5% stake in the 588 MW Beatrice Offshore Wind Farm for approximately £155 million on October 29, lifting its holding to 35%. SSE Renewables (40%) and Red Rock Renewables (25%) retain the remainder. Beatrice has been operating since 2019 off the Caithness coast.

items.title: Tokyo Century Acquires 50% Stake in 212 MW UK Solar and Wind Portfolio from Egg Power
items.body_html: Tokyo Century agreed to acquire a 50% stake in a 212 MW UK renewable portfolio from Egg Power, comprising a solar farm, a solar development project and a wind farm. The deal adds the Japanese trading and leasing conglomerate to a growing list of Asian corporates building UK clean energy positions ahead of the country’s 2030 clean power target.

items.title: Neighborhood Sun Acquires Meadow Energy and Its New York Community Solar Portfolio—Doubles Portfolio to 600+ MWdc; 30,000+ Subscribers Transferred
items.body_html: Neighborhood Sun acquired Meadow Energy and its New York community solar portfolio, doubling total managed capacity from ~300 MWdc to more than 600 MWdc and quadrupling its New York state presence. The deal transfers 67 Meadow Energy projects and more than 30,000 subscribers to Neighborhood Sun’s platform. Neighborhood Sun now operates across more than 200 community solar projects in Maryland, eight additional states and Washington D.C.

items.title: IGNIS Closes Sale of 656 MWp Italian Renewable Portfolio to flyRen Energy Group—28 Projects; flyRen Now Manages Over 2 GW in Italy
items.body_html: Spanish developer IGNIS closed the sale of 656 MWp across 28 renewable projects in Italy to flyRen Energy Group SpA, majority-owned by Foresight Energy Infrastructure Partners II. With the transaction, flyRen’s managed Italian portfolio surpasses 2 GW.

items.title: Optivolt Raises $32 Million Series A to Scale Module-Level Solar Power Electronics—99.4% Conversion Efficiency Claimed; Total Funding $42 M
items.body_html: Optivolt, a San Francisco startup developing module-level power electronics for solar panels, closed a $32 million Series A led by VXI Capital, with RA Capital, Valo Ventures, Atlas Innovate and former SunPower CEO Tom Werner participating. The company’s Power Balancer claims 99.4% conversion efficiency and recovers output lost to shading and mismatch. Total funding: $42 million.
